210:## Passing secrets to nested workflows
--
212:You can use `jobs.<job_id>.secrets` in a calling workflow to pass named secrets to a directly called workflow. Alternatively, you can use `jobs.<job_id>.secrets.inherit` to pass all of the calling workflow's secrets to a directly called workflow. For more information, see the section [AUTOTITLE](/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/reuse-workflows#passing-inputs-and-secrets-to-a-reusable-workflow) above, and the reference article [AUTOTITLE](/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobsjob_idsecretsinherit). Secrets are only passed to directly called workflow, so in the workflow chain A > B > C, workflow C will only receive secrets from A if they have been passed from A to B, and then from B to C. item.text: {"answer":"`jobs.<job_id>.secrets` in the calling workflow must use secret names that are defined by `on.workflow_call.secrets` in the reusable workflow. GitHub Docs says the secret identifier in the caller \"must match the names defined in the called workflow\"; if you want to pass `github-token`, the reusable workflow must declare `on.workflow_call.secrets.github-token` (or use `secrets: inherit` to pass all caller secrets). Your current reusable workflow only passes `with: github-token: ...` to the action, but it does not define a reusable-workflow secret named `github-token`, so the caller fails validation.","sources":["content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax.md","content/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/reuse-workflows.md"]}
